The agent's response comprehensively addresses all elements of the expected output. It treats output conformance as measurable: it proposes enabling Bedrock invocation logging and running CloudWatch Logs Insights queries to compute a 'fence rate' (share of responses with code fences) by hour and modelId, comparing this week to last week as a baseline — directly matching the requirement to quantify failure rate against a pre-change baseline. It distinguishes real distributional shift from non-determinism implicitly by suggesting comparison across time and model IDs, and explicitly discusses causes: model version/alias update, inference profile/routing change, or parameter change — matching the 'plausible causes' requirement (undocumented model update, version/routing change, generation variability). It recommends enforcement that doesn't depend on model behavior: schema/structured-output enforcement at generation time (layer 1), a tolerant extractor, JSON Schema validation with retry, and critically a parse-failure metric with alarm ('create a metric filter on the fence pattern and alarm on it... have your parser emit a metric tagged by failure reason'). Finally, it explicitly recommends a regression gate: 'Build a golden set of 50-200 representative prompts. In CI, and again whenever the model ID changes, run each prompt several times... block promotion if they don't' — directly matching the regression gate requirement to score format conformance before a model change is promoted. All key elements are present and well-matched.</reasoning>
